title: asyncio Tasks, gather and Concurrent Coroutines

understand.concept: asyncio tasks schedule coroutines to run concurrently on an event loop. create_task schedules a coroutine so it can progress while the current coroutine awaits. gather waits for multiple awaitables and collects their results. Concurrency here is cooperative: tasks share an event-loop thread and switch at await points.
understand.whyItMatters: Scheduling independent I/O tasks together can reduce total waiting time compared with awaiting each operation sequentially.
understand.analogy: A coordinator starts several requests and collects their replies as each request finishes, rather than waiting for each one before starting the next.
understand.analogyLimit: Tasks do not execute Python CPU instructions in parallel on one event-loop thread; cancellation and exceptions must be handled deliberately.
understand.summary: asyncio Tasks, gather and Concurrent Coroutines develops advanced concurrency and performance skills.

explain.narrative:
## Schedule independent work
Use `asyncio.create_task(coro)` to schedule a coroutine to run soon. Await the task to obtain its result. `asyncio.gather()` runs multiple awaitables concurrently and returns results in input order. Tasks can be cancelled, and cancellation should generally be allowed to propagate after cleanup.

Avoid creating unbounded numbers of tasks for huge input collections. Use a semaphore or bounded queue to limit concurrency when the service or system has finite capacity.

examples.title: Run two coroutines with gather
examples.code:
import asyncio
async def value(number):
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return number
async def main():
    return await asyncio.gather(value(2), value(3))
print(asyncio.run(main()))
examples.explanation: gather schedules awaitables and returns their results in the supplied order.

examples.title: Schedule a task explicitly
examples.code:
import asyncio
async def work(): return 'finished'
async def main():
    task = asyncio.create_task(work())
    return await task
print(asyncio.run(main()))
examples.explanation: create_task schedules a coroutine as a Task on the running event loop.

examples.title: Inspect task completion
examples.code:
import asyncio
async def main():
    task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.sleep(0))
    await task
    return task.done()
print(asyncio.run(main()))
examples.explanation: A task's done method reports whether it has completed.

examples.title: Collect results in input order
examples.code:
import asyncio
async def echo(value):
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return value
async def main(): return await asyncio.gather(echo('a'), echo('b'))
print(asyncio.run(main()))
examples.explanation: gather returns results in the order of the awaitables passed to it.

examples.title: Limit concurrency with a semaphore
examples.code:
import asyncio
async def main():
    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(2)
    async with semaphore:
        return semaphore.locked()
print(asyncio.run(main()))
examples.explanation: A semaphore controls how many tasks may enter a protected section concurrently.
